title: Adaptive KV Compression + Swapflow for OOM Mitigation and Low-Latency Fallbacks
creator: Ava Kim
description: Problem: Intermittent OOMs under mixed-length continuous-batching workloads are causing degraded availability for some customers. Current mechanisms rely heavily on hard eviction of KV entries and coarse-grained model fallbacks, which either increase tail latency or produce large quality regressions. Goal: implement a layered runtime that (1) compresses and transiently swaps low-value KV cache entries to CPU/host memory when GPU pressure spikes, (2) performs admission-time lightweight KV compaction based on per-request prefix hit probability, and (3) orchestrates fast, quality-preserving fallbacks to smaller model variants only when memory cannot be reclaimed quickly enough. This ticket covers design, prototype integration in the batch admission path, safety guards, and a staged rollout with observability and rollback controls.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype integrated into runtime admission path and KV manager (feature gated).
OOM incident rate reduced by >= 80% on internal worst-case synthetic workload without increasing p95 latency by more than 15%.
Fallbacks to smaller model variants must preserve at least 90% of baseline quality on our prompt set as measured by automated evals (semantic similarity + task accuracy).
Operational controls (console toggle, per-customer opt-out, throttle limits) exist and are documented.
Automated test coverage for compression correctness and swap/restore paths added to CI.
notes: 2026-02-20 — Kickoff: scoped to 8pts. Design doc drafted in Confluence: /confluence/rw/runtime/kv-swapflow (link internal).

2026-02-24 — Decision: prefer lightweight LZ4-based streaming compression for KV entries to minimize CPU overhead. Rationale: GPU memory savings vs CPU cost trade-off favorable for short-lived spikes. (Design note).

2026-02-28 — Trade-offs discussed with Priya Desai (PM): compressing too aggressively hurts prefix hit latency for hot prefixes. Agreed to implement hot/cold tagging and only compress candidate cold entries.

2026-03-03 — Prototype: added compress-on-evict path that serializes cold KV entries into pinned host memory and records a compact index. Basic restore path implemented. Benchmark: compression+swap adds median +1.8ms on restore path under microbench (host restore), acceptable for our SLA when used as fallback path.

2026-03-05 — Integration: admission controller updated to compute a per-request KV salvage score using existing prefix hit estimator and request token budget. Requests with low salvage score are routed into a fast-fallback pipeline that either (a) trims non-critical KV entries, (b) triggers compress-and-swap of selected entries, or (c) if memory still insufficient, triggers model-variant swap.

2026-03-07 — Safety: implemented a two-phase memory reclaim sequence — (1) compress-and-swap of cold KV, (2) preemptive KV compaction, (3) model-variant swap. Each phase has observability and can be short-circuited by the orchestrator if reclaim succeeds earlier.

2026-03-09 — Observability: added metrics: kv_swap_rate, kv_swap_restore_latency_ms, kv_compression_ratio, oom_recoveries_by_phase, fallback_model_routing_pct. Exposed traces for swap/restore in console and added an alert: oom_recoveries_by_phase > 0.1% sustained triggers on-call.

2026-03-10 — Perf tests: stress harness with mixed short/long prompts (80/20) for 6h. Results: OOMs went from 12/hour to 1.8/hour, p95 latency increased from 210ms to 235ms (12%); token cost delta +3.5%. Meets initial SLA targets. Need more long-run tests with real customer prompt distributions.

2026-03-11 — Review feedback from infra: ensure CPU throttling protections; compression must yield configurable CPU caps per node. Added per-node cpu_budget setting and fallback to immediate model swap if we cannot compress within budget.

2026-03-12 — Security review note: swapping KV to host memory keeps content in memory (not on-disk) and respects KMS policies; confirm no persistence to local disk. Security team comfortable with runtime-only swap when feature gated and logged.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Week 1-2): Implement compress-and-swap primitives in KV manager, add LZ4 compressor, add pinned host memory allocator and index metadata.
Phase 2 (Week 3): Integrate admission controller salvage scoring and safe reclaim sequence; add orchestrator hooks for two-phase reclaim.
Phase 3 (Week 4): Add model-variant fast-swap path, QA tests, and end-to-end monitoring dashboards and runbooks.
Phase 4 (Week 5): Canary rollout to internal dedicated cluster, then to low-traffic hosted customers behind feature flag. Collect quality metrics and rollback if eval drops >10% on safety set.
Phase 5 (Week 6): Gradual ramp; final opt-in for Dedicated customers. Post-mortem and retention policy for swap metadata.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Compression CPU spikes may starve inference; Mitigation: enforce cpu_budget for compression and fallback to model-swap when budget exceeded.
Risk: Restore latency on hot prefixes could add tail latency; Mitigation: hot/cold tagging using recent-hit counters, never compress hot entries; prefetch expected restores for in-flight requests.

Risk: Quality regression when swapping to smaller model; Mitigation: evaluate candidate model variants on representative prompts and use hybrid response where top-k tokens are fetched from both models if enabled.
Risk: Operational complexity; Mitigation: expose controls in console (per-customer toggle, thresholds), and provide clear runbooks and automated rollback hooks.

Add CPU-budget configuration to node agent and ensure enforcement in CI (SRE pairing).
Run 48h canary in internal cluster with production-like traffic and collect fallback model quality data.
